edbDesc: A specific type of photoluminescence related to fluorescence. Unlike fluorescence, a phosphorescent material does not immediately re-emit the radiation it absorbs.
title: Phosphorescence
description: Some materials soak up light and keep glowing after the light goes off, slowly fading over minutes or hours. In 1602 Vincenzo Cascariolo, a Bologna shoemaker and alchemist, baked a stone that glowed in the dark after sitting in sunlight, the 'Bologna stone'. Glow-in-the-dark watch dials, power-free exit signs, toys and long-glow radar screens use it.
effect: a material stores absorbed light and slowly gives it back as a glow in the dark
usedIn: Photoluminescent exit signs that need no power
Long-persistence phosphor screens in radar displays
strength: Modern strontium aluminate pigment, charged by ten minutes of light, stays visible in the dark for up to about 10 hours, though dimly.
pickWhy: Borderline: Judgment call: strictly a variant of photoluminescence, so e4 could merge it into Fluorescence; picked keep as its own card because its afterglow does a different job (storing light for hours).
